In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic field in blazars is highly disordered at all scales, and that the jet structure is not aligned with the magnetic field, but the latter is aligned with the jet direction.

blazars are highly complex and variable objects, and that the millimeter linear polarization is a good tracer of the magnetic field orientation, which is progressively better ordered as the jet region becomes more upstream.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
millimeter jets are more ordered, less variable and less depolarized than their radio counterparts.

the magnetic field in blazar jets is better ordered and the linear polarization is higher at the jet innermost regions, but the jet magnetic field is not preferentially oriented in either parallel or transverse directions with regard to the jet axis, and it is variable at time scales of months and years, both in total flux and polarization.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the millimeter emission in blazar jets comes from a region where the magnetic field is progressively better ordered with respect to the radio emission.
the linear polarization degree is significantly higher in the millimeter range than in the centimeter range, and that this excess is not due to a selection effect.
